title: fix(rest): the /security routes answer from the request's environment kernel on a hosted runtime, so an owner can accept an installed app's default permission set (#30192)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP36dhgMaYCeGkfLNzbkur4f)_

Part of #30192 · Refs #29999 · follows #30011 (PR #30013) · unblocks objectstack-ai/cloud#3560

The card carries no `Claim:` naming this branch, so this body declares `Part of`; the owning seat closes the card by hand once this lands.

## What changes

**The card's fix.** `securityServiceProvider` in `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` is now `environmentScopedProvider<ISecurityService>('security')`, the seam #30013 introduced, with the same legs and the same rule: a request for environment A is answered by A's `security` service or by nothing, never by the host's.

**Every consumer asks for the request's environment.** As #30013 did for its five, each route that reads the `security` seam now passes the id `RestServer.resolveRequestEnvironmentId` answered (the scoped param, else the host's `kernel-resolver` for a hostname-routed request):

- `security-routes.ts`, suggested bindings (list, confirm, dismiss, reopen): the resolver passed the raw route param, which is `undefined` on the unscoped mount. It now resolves the request's environment first. `SecurityRouteHost` gains `resolveRequestEnvironmentId`.
- `security-routes.ts`, `security/explain` and `my-delegable-scope`: the resolver read the environment's kernel and then fell back to the host provider. It now asks the provider for the resolved id and nothing else, the shape `analytics-routes.ts` took in #30013. `SecurityExplainRouteHost` drops `kernelManager`, which nothing reads any more.
- `RestServer.resolveSecurityService` (the record page's field-access and explain parts, `/data/:object/:id/field-access`, the export door's permission check and readable-field projection, the import template's gates and projection, and the object-schema field masker behind the meta object reads): same change as explain. On a healthy hosted environment these already read the environment's service first, so what changes is that the host no longer answers when the environment's kernel does not.
- `RestServer.metaReadAudienceSources().resolveSecurityService` (the meta read gate's permission-set audiences): passed the raw id; now passes the resolved one.

**The audit the card asked for.** Verdicts for the remaining providers in the same block:

| Provider | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `security` | environment-scoped | The card's fix. plugin-security registers `security` on the environment's kernel (`ArtifactKernelFactory` mounts `SecurityPlugin` per environment) and the hosted host kernel has none, so every `/security` door answered 501. |
| `settings` | **environment-scoped** | Wrong on every hosted request today. `computeExecCtx` localizes (time zone, locale, currency) through this provider and passed it the resolved id, but the provider ignored it and read the host's `settings`. The hosted host is a routing shell, and `settings` lives on each environment kernel (`HOSTED_FORCED_REQUIRES` in cloud). The runtime dispatcher's execution context already reads the request kernel's `settings`, so the REST face and the dispatcher face localized the same caller differently. |
| `auth` | **environment-scoped** | Latent. `computeExecCtx` reads the environment kernel's `auth` first and reaches this provider only when that answered nothing, which includes an `auth` factory that faulted (`seamOrUndefined` folds the fault into `undefined`). The provider then answered with the host's `auth`, and `computeExecCtx` recorded the session as the environment's (`authEnvironmentId = environmentId`). Identity is per environment (ADR-0006), so that request must be authenticated by nobody. |
| `i18n` | **environment-scoped** | Latent. `resolveI18nService` reads the environment kernel first; when it answered nothing, the provider translated with the host's bundle. Its own docblock says the platform kernel does not own per-app bundles. |
| `metadata` | **environment-scoped** | Latent. `resolveEndpointMatchAuthority` and `resolveMetadataService` read the environment kernel first; when it answered nothing, the host's matcher judged the environment's endpoint faces against the host's own `api` items (Route & surface ownership rule 4). Absence is now absence, which those faces already report loudly. |
| `tenancy` | host, comment added | Right as it is. Every consumer reads the bound environment kernel's `tenancy` first (`computeExecCtx`'s kernel branch, `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy`), so only a request in no environment, or a single kernel, ever reaches this provider. |

For `auth`, `i18n` and `metadata` nothing changes on cloud's hosted runtime as composed today: every environment kernel carries all three (`FACTORY_INLINE_CAPABILITIES` lists `auth` and `i18n`, and a real `ObjectKernel` injects in-memory `i18n` and `metadata` fallbacks). The change removes the host as an answer when one of them is missing or faults. The consumers of these four already pass the resolved id, so only the providers changed.

Changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/rest`.

## Why

On cloud's hosted runtime one `RestApiPlugin` sits on the host kernel in front of every environment kernel. The `/security` provider read the host's `security` service whatever environment it was asked for, and the unscoped suggested-binding mount asked it for no environment at all. The host has no such service, so `GET/POST /api/v1/security/suggested-bindings[/:id/confirm]` answered 501 「Security service is not configured on this deployment」. No owner could accept an installed app's default permission set (HotCRM's `crm_user`), and every invited member read 403 on the app's data (coordinator reading on #29999, cloud#3560). #30013 fixed five sibling providers and left this one out.

## Verification

Readings on `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, branch `claude/project-thread-s1jtte`, in a cloud container. The two test files were run at `e6a3d8fc` (branched from `b7075d99`), and the suite was run again after merging `main` at `474c030b` (head `dec05a8f`).

**`rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts`** (#30013's harness; new pins added there as top-level `describe`s, per the shared-harness rule). Real `ObjectKernel`s: a host with the real plugin, `kernel-manager` and `kernel-resolver`, in front of environment kernels, each registering its occupants in a plugin `init`. The host carries its own occupant of every slot, so an answer from the host is seen:

- Three new `DOORS` rows (`GET /security/suggested-bindings`, `POST /security/suggested-bindings/:id/confirm`, `GET /security/explain`) go through #30013's whole matrix. On the scoped and hostname mounts, for env A and env B, each is answered by exactly one call on the target environment's service, never the host's or the other environment's. An environment with no `security` service gets the door's own 501, and the host is not asked. In a single-kernel composition (no `kernel-manager`) the same doors are answered by the one kernel, unchanged.
- Env A's suggestion cannot be confirmed through env B on either mount. B's service is asked and answers 404 `SUGGESTION_NOT_FOUND`.
- A new `describe` covers the audited seams on the hosted shape, with the host carrying its own `auth` (a `u_host` session), `settings` (its own time zone), `i18n` and `metadata`. An environment kernel with no `auth` authenticates nobody. The execution context's `timezone` is env A's (`Asia/Tokyo`) and env B's (`Europe/Paris`) on both mounts, never the host's. `resolveI18nService` and `resolveMetadataService` return the environment's occupant, or `undefined` for an environment without one. `resolveSecurityService` and the meta gate's `resolveSecurityService` reach the environment's service, or `undefined`.

**`rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`**: the scope table now marks `auth`, `i18n`, `settings`, `security` and `metadata` as environment-scoped. Each is asked of `env_1`'s kernel for `env_1`, and of the plugin's own for no id and for `platform`. With no `kernel-manager`, all ten environment-scoped providers read the plugin's own kernel for every id.

| | the two files (95 cases) |
|---|---|
| **ablation**: `rest-api-plugin.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `security-routes.ts` restored to `b7075d99` | **21 red**: every suggested-binding list and confirm case (8), the three absent-service cases on each mount (the host answered), the cross-environment confirm, the four audited-seam cases, and two slot-table cases. The seam readings: auth answered `u_host`; env A's `timezone` read `America/New_York` (the host's); a bare environment's `i18n` answered `{ __env: 'host' }`; the hostname meta gate reached the host's `security`. |
| **this branch** | **95 green** |

The explain door's served cases passed on the ablated tree too, because its resolver already read the environment's kernel first. Its absent-service cases failed there, because it fell back to the host.

**Suites and gates.** `@objectstack/rest`: 391 files, 7,560 passed, 352 skipped, 0 failed, before and after the `main` merge. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` is clean, including `check:test-typecheck`. `eslint` is clean on the five files. These gates are green: `check:slot-lookup`, `check:service-providers`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:changeset-fixed`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:rest-log-declared`, `check:rest-log-spy-declared`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:symbol-anchors`, `check:adr-anchors`, `check:issue-citations` and `check:route-ledger-census`.

**Not proven here.** The card's done-when has two more steps: on a real hosted environment with plugin-security and HotCRM installed, a `manage_metadata` holder confirms `crm_user` and the invited member then reads the app's data. Both run on cloud's side, in cloud#3560's pin round. The tests above pin which kernel answers. plugin-security's own gating and re-derivation of `everyone` are unchanged and not re-tested here.

**Noted for the lane, not changed** (outside the card's list, not measured on a hosted runtime): `objectQLProvider` reads the plugin's own kernel whatever id it is handed. Four consumers call it with an environment id: the transactional `POST /batch` (`batch-routes.ts`), `meta-object-state-routes.ts`, `meta-item-history-routes.ts`, and the meta read gate's `isItemOfDisabledPackage`. `computeExecCtx` already reads the environment kernel's `objectql`. These look like candidates for the same audit. Also, as #30013's review noted, the request's environment is resolved twice per request (once in `resolveExecCtx`, once for the provider). These doors follow that pattern.

Metadata-protocol: none
